causes.text: Intel signaled it might exit its chip manufacturing operations if it failed to secure major customers, reported a larger-than-expected quarterly loss, and paused work at its Hillsboro plant due to high costs, prompting its shares to sink more than 8%.

source_info.title: Intel slumps as potential foundry exit deepens investor gloom

effects.text: As Intel's shares tumbled on the news, AMD shares climbed over 2.6% as investors anticipated that Intel's strategic uncertainty and market-share losses would benefit AMD.

source_info.title: Intel shares slide on quarterly loss, foundry business exit risk

causal_reasoning_chain.description: On July 25, 2025, Intel announced a bigger-than-expected loss, suggested it could exit its manufacturing operations if it failed to secure a major customer, and temporarily halted work at a factory due to excessive costs.
These announcements increased uncertainty about Intel's competitive strategy and financial health, raising concerns that it would lose market share to rivals.
Investors anticipated that AMD, as Intel's primary competitor in CPUs and data-center chips, would capture some of Intel's market share.
As a result, AMD's stock price increased by roughly 2.6% while Intel's shares slumped more than 8%.

rationale: Reuters reported that AMD's shares rose as Intel signaled weakness in its foundry strategy and posted a sharp quarterly loss, prompting capital reallocation toward AMD.
counterfactual_analysis: If Intel had not raised the possibility of exiting manufacturing and reported a loss, investors may not have shifted capital into AMD, and AMD's stock would likely have remained level.

adversarial_confounders.text: Speculation about AMD's upcoming earnings and AI momentum.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Positive expectations for AMD's own performance could have boosted the stock independently of Intel's news.

adversarial_confounders.text: Overall market movements such as the NASDAQ rising on macroeconomic news.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Broader market trends might have influenced AMD's share price.

details.commentary: EU digital rules and enforcement lowered some structural advantages that had helped large platforms like Amazon deter smaller rivals. By forcing changes to self-preferencing and data use, regulators effectively made it easier for local marketplaces and merchants to compete for European shoppers.
